title: Runtime probe-weighted SLO burn-rate adjuster and noise-aware paging shield
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Fluctuating background traffic and noisy synthetic probes cause burn-rate alerts to fire too frequently for low-severity degradation. On-call teams are paged for transient blips (prefix cache warm-ups, seed traffic, background replays), increasing toil and desensitizing responders. Goal: implement a burn-rate adjustment layer that weights probe types and stabilizes short-window SLO calculations, plus a noise-aware paging shield that suppresses pages for low-impact anomalies while preserving visibility in dashboards and automated remediation paths.
acceptance_criteria: Weighted burn-rate computation is available as a queryable metric (burn_rate.weighted) for both request- and token-based SLOs
Short-window (1m/5m) alert noise reduced by >= 45% on the pilot services without increasing time-to-detect for sustained degradations
Paging shield suppresses P1 pages for anomalies tagged as 'probe' or 'low-impact' but emits a non-pager alert channel (ops-quiet) with full context
Dashboards show both raw and adjusted burn-rate curves with explainability metadata (probe weights and contributing traces)
Rollout can be toggled per-service via feature flags and per-route config in the console
implementation_notes: Add 'probe_type' tag to tracing hooks and metrics ingest path (supported values: production, synthetic, background_replay, canary)

Introduce a lightweight transform in the metrics pipeline that computes weighted_error = error_count * weight(probe_type) and exposes burn_rate.weighted = sum(weighted_error)/sum(weighted_requests) over windows
Default weights: production=1.0, canary=0.6, background_replay=0.2, synthetic=0.1. Weights configurable via feature flags and service-level overrides

Implement noise-aware paging shield as an alert routing policy: evaluate (burn_rate.weighted, anomaly_score, probe_density) -> decision {page|ops-quiet|ignore}. Thresholds stored in console per-environment
Preserve raw alerting condition pipeline so customers can opt into strict paging if desired
Update probe-enrichment library in runtime to attach probe metadata earlier (before sidecar aggregation) to reduce loss of attribution
test_plan: Unit tests for transform: validate weighting arithmetic, zero-division safeguards, and stable-window semantics
Integration test: synthetic ingestion pipeline with mixed probe traffic verifying burn_rate.weighted and raw burn_rate outputs
Canary rollout to staging: enable weighting for internal staging services and verify alert suppression behavior under controlled noise injection
Chaos test: generate sustained real errors to ensure weighted burn-rate still crosses pager thresholds for genuine outages
Simulate oncall load: run a 2-week shadow of the paging shield to measure reduction in pages and false-positive rate
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): feature branches, unit + integration tests, internal library updates (1 week)
Phase 1 (staging): enable for observability-internal services, run controlled injection experiments (1 week)
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for three customer-facing services with differing traffic shapes, measure noise and time-to-detect (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): opt-in per-team via console toggles, collect feedback and iterate on default weights (4 weeks)
Rollback: disable feature flag or set all weights to 1.0 to return to raw burn-rate behavior
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Patel: Created ticket after postmortem showed 18 pages in 72h attributable to synthetic probe spikes. Proposed weighting model and paging shield to reduce churn.

2026-03-04 Ethan Zhou: Spiked a prototype transform in local metrics pipeline; basic weighting arithmetic looks fine but need to confirm tag fidelity in tracing hooks. Filed small follow-up ENG-146783 for hook instrumentation gaps.

2026-03-06 SRE Lead (Sofia Martínez): Concern: suppressing pages risks missing true regressions when probe density is low. Suggest adding anomaly_score floor and mandatory pager for high-severity anomalies regardless of probe tag.

2026-03-08 Design Review (Liam O'Connor): Dashboard mockups reviewed — we should surface probe composition as stacked area under burn-rate curve and provide hover drilldowns to representative traces/PRs.
2026-03-10 QA (Priya Nair): Integration tests passing in CI, but observed slight lag (200-300ms) in transform when probe tag is missing — adding defensive fallback to treat untagged as production.
2026-03-12 Ethan Zhou: Deployed staging canary. Initial telemetry: alerts reduced by ~52% on staging service A, time-to-detect for sustained 5m degradation unchanged. Preparing pilot onboarding docs.
2026-03-14 Maya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include console toggles and explainability metadata. Scheduling retro with oncall rotation to tune thresholds after pilot week.
